method.selection_policy: LLM-selected market-relevant items from news_digest.json; preserves source metadata and excludes noise.

framework.Equities: Broad equity/risk sentiment; market-moving mega-cap/AI allowed; low-signal single-stock noise excluded.
framework.Commodities: Physical commodity futures framework; supply disruption/demand strength positive; supply increase/demand weakness negative.
framework.FX: USD-centric basket; non-USD currency strength positive; USD/DXY strength negative.
framework.Rates: Bond-price framework; yields up/selloff/higher-for-longer negative; yields down/bond rally/cooler inflation positive.

Equities.title: Tech stocks surge as Micron earnings ease AI fears, oil falls further
Equities.reason: Representative broad-market piece: Micron earnings triggered a tech-led risk-on move and eased AI demand worries. Dominant equity narrative = AI/chip leadership driving market upside, so strong positive directional bias and high relevance.

Equities.title: Nasdaq futures jump 2% as Micron, Qualcomm forecasts relieve investors
Equities.reason: Market-open/futures move: shows immediate risk-on reaction and breadth (Nasdaq/S&P futures); reinforces that tech/AI leadership is the dominant near-term market driver — meaningful positive impact on equity risk sentiment.

Equities.title: Micron stock jumps over 16% in premarket trading after blockbuster earnings
Equities.summary: The company's revenue more than quadrupled from $9.3 billion a year earlier to $41.46 billion, it reported on Wednesday
Equities.reason: Idiosyncratic-but-systemic: large upside at a bellwether chip name materially alters the 'AI memory' trade narrative and lifts sentiment across tech — positive for broad tech leadership, but single-company detail lowers relevance vs. macro pieces.

Equities.title: Stocks Rally as Micron Buoys AI Trade Ahead of PCE: Markets Wrap
Equities.reason: Macro wrap: ties Micron-driven tech strength into broader market context (ahead of PCE). Reinforces narrative that tech/AI momentum is the primary market impulse, supporting risk-on positioning into macro data.

Equities.title: Global tech stocks rebound after Micron’s profit surge
Equities.summary: US chipmaker’s bumper quarterly profits calm investor fears after market sell-off this week
Equities.reason: Analyst/feature piece: frames Micron as calming investor fears after recent weakness. Useful context on sentiment and leadership but slightly lower relevance than immediate-flow headlines.

Equities.title: Qualcomm stock pops 15% after chipmaker almost doubles projection for 2029 non-handset revenue
Equities.summary: Qualcomm's primary business has been smartphones, which accounted for two-thirds of the company's product revenue in it's most recent quarter.
Equities.reason: Complementary signal: another major chip/tech name upgrading long-term AI/enterprise revenue outlook — supports the cohesive AI narrative but is more company-specific so slightly lower relevance.

Rates.title: Indian Rupee: Gains constrained against US Dollar – Societe Generale
Rates.summary: Societe Generale notes that Indian money markets have continued to unwind tightening expectations, with the 1-year swap rate dropping to 5.75% and the 10-year IGB yield easing to 6.80%.
Rates.reason: Local money-market and government yield easing (1y swap and 10y IGB) implies a bond rally in India (yields down = positive for Rates). Moderate relevance as it is country-specific EM rates.

Rates.title: US core PCE inflation expected to rise in May amid hawkish Fed expectations
Rates.summary: The United States (US) Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) will publish the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index data for May on Thursday at 12:30 GMT.
Rates.reason: Core PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge; upside surprise increases hawkish Fed expectations and pushes yields higher (bond-negative). High relevance for global rates and policy path.

Rates.title: PBOC Plans Overnight Reverse Repo in Next Stage of Policy Shift
Rates.reason: Introducing/expanding reverse repo operations is likely to drain liquidity and put upward pressure on short-term Chinese rates (bond-negative). Material for domestic money markets and EM rates.

Rates.title: BOJ’s Tamura Calls for Raising Interest Rate Every Few Months
Rates.reason: A BOJ official calling for repeated rate increases signals a hawkish tilt and upward pressure on JGB yields (negative for bond prices). High relevance given BOJ's market impact.

Rates.title: Japan’s 20-Year Bond Sale Sees Weakest Demand in Over a Year
Rates.reason: Weak demand at a long-dated JGB auction suggests issuance pressure and prospective higher yields (bond-negative). Direct market signal for supply/demand in government bonds.

Rates.title: China Starts Marketing Record €5 Billion of Sovereign Bonds
Rates.reason: Record-sized sovereign euro issuance increases supply and can put upward pressure on yields; modest relevance to global fixed-income supply dynamics.

Rates.title: China Pushes Rating Firms to Review AAA Glut in Bond Market
Rates.reason: Regulatory pressure on ratings and potential repricing of AAA supply could increase uncertainty and risk premia in China's bond market (mildly bond-negative).

Rates.title: UK sells £1.5 billion of treasury gilts maturing in 2029
Rates.reason: Routine gilt issuance increases supply; modest upward pressure on yields for the curve segment (bond-negative, low-medium relevance).

Rates.title: Asset Purchase Facility: Gilt Sales – Market Notice 19 June 2026
Rates.summary: This Market Notice sets out the schedule for sales in Q3 2026 of gilts held in the Asset Purchase Facility (APF) for monetary policy purposes.
Rates.reason: Planned APF gilt sales are a form of QT and remove central-bank support for gilt prices, implying higher gilt yields (material for UK rates).

Rates.title: Federal Reserve Board and Federal Open Market Committee release economic projections from the June 16-17 FOMC meeting
Rates.summary: Federal Reserve Board and Federal Open Market Committee release economic projections from the June 16-17 FOMC meeting
Rates.reason: FOMC economic projections shape the expected path of fed funds; a projection consistent with higher-for-longer or slower disinflation is bond-negative (pushes yields up). High relevance for global rates.

Rates.title: ECB to integrate non-financial credit claim portfolios into general collateral framework, phasing out temporary measures
Rates.reason: Integrating credit claims into the GC framework should ease collateral shortages and improve market functioning, supporting European bond prices (yields down = positive for Rates).

Rates.title: Philippine Bond Relief Rally Is Meeting Institutional Skepticism
Rates.reason: A recent relief rally in Philippine bonds is noted but met with skepticism; mild positive price action for local bonds but limited confidence/relevance.

Rates.title: Plan for the Outright Purchases of Japanese Government Bonds
Rates.reason: BOJ outright purchase plans are direct supportive action for JGBs (buying supply => yields down). High relevance for JGB market mechanics.

FX.title: ECB’s Schnabel: Interest rates need to raise further to bring inflation down to 2% target
FX.summary: European Central Bank (ECB) policymaker Isabel Schnabel reiterates that the central bank is not done with monetary tightening yet, according to her remarks released by Econostream released during the European trading session on Thursday.
FX.reason: ECB official signalling further hikes supports EUR vs USD (tightening differential narrative). High relevance for FX as ECB rate-hike rhetoric counters USD-strength/backdrop around PCE.

FX.title: Japanese Yen: PCE shocks drive intraday moves against US Dollar – MUFG
FX.summary: MUFG analysts stress that USD/JPY is highly sensitive to United States (US) Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index surprises, especially in the current environment of Fed focus on inflation persistence.
FX.reason: Notes USD/JPY sensitivity to US PCE — implies potential USD strength shocks pressuring JPY intraday. Useful short-term FX signal but limited directional conviction until PCE print.

FX.title: Canadian Dollar languishes at 14-month lows amid Fed hiking bets, lower Oil prices
FX.summary: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) consolidates losses on Thursday, as the US Dollar (USD) remains buoyed by heightened hopes that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will tighten its monetary policy later this year.
FX.reason: USD strength / Fed-hike pricing is the dominant driver pushing USD/CAD higher; falling oil adds downside to CAD. Material for USD-centric FX flows and CAD rates/yield differentials.

FX.title: United States Dollar Index holds above 101.50 ahead of US PCE inflation
FX.summary: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, continues its winning streak for the fourth successive day and is trading around 101.60 during the European hours on Thursday.
FX.reason: DXY strength ahead of PCE is a high‑signal USD-centric macro theme (risk to non‑USD pairs). Elevated relevance — core market driver for FX positioning.

FX.title: Indian Rupee gains as easing energy supply concerns push oil prices to pre-war levels
FX.summary: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades firmly against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday. The USD/INR pair declines to near 94.30 as the Indian currency strengthens due to a further decline in oil prices.
FX.reason: Oil-driven INR strength vs USD — commodity-to-FX transmission for an EM currency. Relevant to EMUSD flows but smaller market than G7 pairs.

FX.title: Canadian Dollar: High USD/CAD seen as exaggerated – Commerzbank
FX.summary: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister notes that USD/CAD has surged from below 1.36 to above 1.42 as falling Oil prices and rising Fed hike expectations pressured the Canadian Dollar (CAD).
FX.reason: House view that USD/CAD overshot implies potential CAD correction vs USD; medium-low relevance as it's an analyst take countering the prevailing USD‑strength narrative.

FX.title: US Dollar: Consumer resilience and GDP under scrutiny – UBS
FX.summary: UBS’s Chief Economist Paul Donovan focuses on United States (US) consumers ahead of May income and spending data, stressing their persistent willingness to spend despite tariff and Oil price shocks.
FX.reason: Emphasises US consumer resilience underpinning USD — supports USD vs major currencies ahead of data. Relevant for near‑term FX direction.

FX.title: Polish Zloty: NBP dovishness keeps Zloty pressured against Euro – ING
FX.summary: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky highlights persistent Polish Zloty weakness versus Central and Eastern European (CEE) peers as EUR/PLN breaks above its prior range toward 4.290. He attributes vulnerability to the National Bank of Poland’s (NBP) dovish stance and glob
FX.reason: NBP dovishness is a clear local central‑bank driver pushing EUR/PLN higher (EUR strength vs PLN). Relevant for CEE FX flows and ECB/CEE rate differentials.

FX.title: Euro: Stabilising above 1.1300 against US Dollar with risk driver – ING
FX.summary: ING’s Francesco Pesole says calmer markets are allowing the Euro (EUR) to pause against the strong US Dollar (USD), with AI-related sentiment now the main driver for EUR/USD. He expects that if risk stabilisation continues and equities firm, the pair could slo
FX.reason: Highlights EUR stabilisation conditional on risk sentiment — signals potential EUR resilience vs USD if risk-on holds. Useful for EUR/USD short-term outlook ahead of macro prints.

FX.title: Australian Dollar: Oversold but vulnerable against US Dollar – UOB
FX.summary: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note AUD/USD’s sharp fall to 0.6883 before a modest recovery to 0.6901, with deeply oversold conditions pointing to near-term range trading between 0.6880 and 0.6920.
FX.reason: AUD remains vulnerable to USD strength; technical/near‑term note (oversold/range) so moderate relevance for immediate FX flows.

FX.title: US Dollar: Cooler core PCE risks and peak rally view – ING
FX.summary: ING’s Francesco Pesole argues the Dollar rally may be nearing its peak as calmer risk sentiment and softer Federal Reserve (Fed) pricing take hold.
FX.reason: Analyst view that USD rally may be peaking — implies non‑USD currencies could regain ground if PCE is softer. Medium relevance as it provides a counter‑narrative to USD strength.

FX.title: Euro remains pinned near 13-month lows following soft German consumer confidence
FX.summary: The Euro (EUR) edges lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday, extending its decline for the fourth consecutive day.
FX.reason: German confidence data feeds EUR weakness vs USD — reinforces USD‑strength narrative and macro headwinds for EUR in near term.

FX.title: Japanese Yen: Seen weaker against US Dollar – UOB
FX.summary: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report that USD/JPY remains in a range near recent highs, with intraday trading expected between 161.40 and 161.90 after a 161.46–161.83 session.
FX.reason: UOB view of continued JPY weakness vs USD — consistent with broad USD‑strength narrative and relevant for FX and JPY intervention watch.

FX.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Aims to extend rally towards one-year high at around 0.8170
FX.summary: The USD/CHF pair trades 0.16% lower at around 0.8110 during the European trading session on Thursday after correcting from its 10-month high of 0.8140 posted the previous day. The broader outlook of the Swiss Franc pair remains firm due to continued outperform
FX.reason: USD/CHF forecast points to further USD strength vs CHF — relevant to G10 FX positioning and safe‑haven flows into USD rather than CHF.

FX.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecasts: Pound bounces up to 213.40 with intervention risks increasing
FX.summary: The British Pound (GBP) trims losses against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on Thursday, with the GBP/JPY pair trading around 213.40 after bouncing from lows near 212.50 on Wednesday.
FX.reason: Non‑USD cross flagged due to rising intervention risk on JPY — notable for global FX/central‑bank spillovers. Direction reflects GBP strength vs JPY; intervention risk increases monitoring priority.

FX.title: Yen At Historic Low Set to Hand Japan Carmakers $5.8 Billion
FX.reason: Headline indicates JPY at historic low (significant JPY weakness). High relevance for FX given corporate FX exposure and potential policy/intervention implication.

Commodities.title: Oil Prices Fall Toward Prewar Levels as Gulf Shipping Resumes
Commodities.reason: Resumption of tanker movements through the Strait of Hormuz materially eases immediate supply disruption risk from the Iran war, weighing on crude prices and driving the market back toward prewar levels — a significant bearish driver for oil.

Commodities.title: Saudis Set to Restart Ras Tanura Oil Exports as Gulf Flows Rise
Commodities.reason: Restart of a major Saudi export terminal increases physical flows into the market, reducing the war-related risk premium and putting downward pressure on Brent and related crude benchmarks.

Commodities.title: Oil prices erase wartime gains as supply concerns ease with Hormuz tanker traffic resuming
Commodities.summary: Oil prices fell as investors bet global crude supplies will improve, as tankers stranded in the Persian Gulf for months have begun leaving the Strait of Hormuz.
Commodities.reason: Market reaction piece reinforcing that renewed tanker traffic is prompting traders to price out a large portion of the wartime premium — a clear near-term bearish impulse for crude.

Commodities.title: U.S. commercial crude oil inventories have decreased in June
Commodities.summary: For the week ending June 19, 2026, U.S. refineries processed 17.1 million barrels per day (b/d) of crude oil, down 81,000 b/d from the previous week, and they operated at 96.1% capacity utilization. Gasoline production averaged 9.5 million b/d, and distillate
Commodities.reason: Weekly draw in U.S. commercial crude inventories is supportive for West Texas Intermediate and reflects tightening domestic balances, a modest bullish counterpoint to Gulf-flow-driven weakness.

Commodities.title: Permian natural gas production increased faster than crude oil
Commodities.summary: The Permian region's marketed natural gas production grew from 17.2 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) in 2021 to 27.6 Bcf/d in 2025, a 60% increase, according to data from our latest Short Term Energy Outlook. Over the same period, crude oil production grew b
Commodities.reason: Rapid growth in Permian gas supply increases downward pressure on U.S. natural gas prices and reflects structural production trends that are bearish for Henry Hub in the near–medium term.

Commodities.title: Drones Target Russian City With Three Rosneft Oil Refineries
Commodities.reason: Attacks on refinery infrastructure introduce renewed supply-disruption risk for refined products and crude processing capacity in Russia, a supportive (bullish) shock for oil and product markets — however currently a localized counter-signal to Gulf flow normalization.

Commodities.title: UAE's exit from OPEC+ reduced the group's share of crude oil production and capacity
Commodities.summary: On April 28, 2026, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) announced that it was leaving OPEC, effective on May 1. OPEC was formed in 1960 by Iraq, Iran, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela, with the stated objective to "coordinate and unify petroleum policies among Me
Commodities.reason: UAE exit reduces OPEC+'s consolidated production/capacity share and can alter group coordination dynamics, a structural factor that tends to support prices by reducing the effective supply-management capacity of the cartel.

Commodities.title: Iraq Might Leave OPEC If Its Production Quota Isn’t Raised
Commodities.reason: Statements about Iraq potentially exiting OPEC add to political/coordination uncertainty around OPEC quotas; marginally supportive for prices as it signals risks to group cohesion, but currently low immediate market impact.

Commodities.title: Copper Climbs as Lower Dollar, AI Rally Counter Rate Concerns
Commodities.reason: Improving demand tone (AI-driven industrial demand) combined with a softer dollar is supportive for copper prices and offsets some interest-rate headwinds — a constructive signal for industrial metals.

Commodities.title: Gold Steadies Near $4,000 as Stronger Dollar, Rate Outlook Weigh
Commodities.reason: Stronger dollar and firmer rate outlook undermine gold's 'debasing' narrative and reduce bullion's appeal as an inflation/FX hedge, producing a meaningful bearish impulse for precious metals.

Commodities.title: Gold holds below $4,000, silver below $60 — has the shimmer worn off the precious metal rally?
Commodities.summary: Gold is down almost 8% so far this year, while silver has shed more than 20%.
Commodities.reason: Broad pullback in both gold and silver reflects the unwind of speculative 'debasement' trades amid stronger real rates and dollar strength — a clear bearish theme for precious metals markets.

Commodities.title: Chinese Banks Move to Rein in Retail Gold Trading on Volatility
Commodities.reason: Steps by Chinese banks to restrict retail gold trading reduce a potential source of near-term demand/volatility, exerting modest downward pressure on physical gold flows and sentiment.

Commodities.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD holds losses near $57.50 due to prevailing bearish bias
Commodities.summary: XAG/USD remains weaker for the third consecutive day, trading around $57.40 per troy ounce during the European hours on Thursday. The technical analysis of the daily chart shows that the spot price is moving downwards within the descending channel pattern, ind
Commodities.reason: Technical analysis indicates continued downside momentum for silver in the near term; as a price/technical piece it has limited structural relevance but reinforces the bearish precious-metals narrative.

Crypto.title: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposal to require certain payment stablecoin issuers to maintain an effective customer identification program
Crypto.summary: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposal to require certain payment stablecoin issuers to maintain an effective customer identification program
Crypto.reason: Regulatory clarity and mandatory KYC for payment stablecoins likely increases institutional comfort and on‑ramp legitimacy for stablecoins/crypto payment rails; positive for adoption despite higher compliance costs.

Crypto.title: Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin goes live in Japan after regulatory approval
Crypto.reason: Regulatory approval and launch in a major market is a clear adoption win for a stablecoin product, supporting on‑chain payments and regional regulatory acceptance.

Crypto.title: How a Crypto Exchange Became a Major Hub for Illicit Iranian Cash
Crypto.reason: High‑profile reporting tying an exchange to illicit flows raises enforcement and regulatory risk across the sector, damaging trust and likely prompting scrutiny/controls.

Crypto.title: SecondFi loses $2.4 million in Cardano wallet exploit
Crypto.reason: A smart‑contract/wallet exploit and potential larger at‑risk sums are a negative for ecosystem security and investor confidence, especially for Cardano/DeFi native flows.

Crypto.title: Live markets: Bitcoin, ether lead $1 billion liquidation losses as AI trade keeps going
Crypto.reason: Large liquidation events signal sharp positioning shifts and vulnerability to cross‑asset flows (AI‑thematic rotation), increasing short‑term downside risk in crypto markets.

Crypto.title: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 as AI trade continues to draw investor interest and capital
Crypto.reason: Price weakness tied to rotation into AI equities highlights cross‑asset capital flows as a dominant near‑term driver, amplifying downside pressure on crypto.

Crypto.title: Trump's refusal to sign housing bill could delay Congress and imperil Clarity Act
Crypto.reason: Political blockage that could delay crypto‑related legislation (Clarity Act) keeps regulatory uncertainty elevated in the U.S., a net negative for policy clarity and institutional flows.

Crypto.title: Upheaval at the Ethereum Foundation has some of crypto’s biggest names feeling bullish
Crypto.reason: Positive developer/influencer reaction to governance changes at a key ecosystem player can underpin constructive sentiment for ETH and DeFi, but remains a more idiosyncratic/medium‑term signal.
